In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact on LISA sensitivity and parameter-estimability of the loss of a few links, as might be expected in the case of laser-link failures.
the study of the LISA sensitivity in the case of loss of a single inter-spacecraft link, and of a single or multiple intra-spacecraft links.
the study of LISA's scientific performance when the number of available links is reduced.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LISA baseline configuration is the best possible one for the science goals that LISA has been designed to pursue, and that the loss of any of its six links would be a major setback.
the loss in performance is small, and that the four-link case should be considered for LISA.
the LISA baseline configuration (with six links) is the best possible one in all the considered cases, and that the five-link and the four-link configurations are not competitive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a four-link LISA configuration would have the same sensitivity as a six-link one, but with a loss in precision of a factor of sqrt2 in the low-frequency band, and of up to ~2 in the high-frequency band.

, for the considered signals, the loss in performance is modest when going from six to five or four links, and is not too different from that obtained in the five and four links cases by removing one or more intra-spacecraft measurements.

the LISA performance in terms of SNR and parameter-estimations precision is only weakly affected by the loss of one or two links, and is not at all affected by the loss or four intra-spacecraft links.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LISA will be a powerful gravitational-wave observatory also in the case of a failure of one or more laser measurements, and that the loss of sensitivity will be small for most sources.
, in case of failure, the loss in performance is modest and, for the most part, can be recovered by extending the observation time.
